questions: Does narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 m reduce max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, or does it add steering_oscillation?
Where in the course does the first off-track event occur (bend size and sharpness), and is it preceded by a line-loss event?
Is the controller's turn saturating at the wheel-command limit (4095) on the sharpest bend, which would mean turn authority is still limiting?
Does progress now move with base_speed, or is it fixed by off-track ends regardless of speed?

intent: Revert to the iteration 1 layout, which scored best (55.1), and change one variable: wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.09 m. A narrower track gives more turn rate per unit of wheel differential, which should cut the max_error that pins every run at the 0.06 m off-track floor. Sensors stay at y=0.05 because y=0.07 cost about 7 points on the s-bend in iteration 2. Body and mass return to iteration 1 values because lower inertia also hurt.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that a longer sensor lead (y=0.07) and lower yaw inertia (shorter, lighter body) hurt the s-bend and slalom, so the iteration 1 layout is the better base. Off-track floor is fixed at 0.06 m across all body widths, so only turn authority and speed can change the outcome. Next: if wheel_track narrowing helps max_error, try 0.08 m. If it hurts oscillation, return to 0.12 m and examine wheel_radius for speed.
rationale: Evidence: every run in every iteration ends off_track, with progress stuck at 0.10 to 0.16 and max_error at 0.060 to 0.068 m, which is the off-track floor. Iteration 1 (7 sensors, 16 mm, y=0.05, body 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg) was the best so far at 55.1. Widening the array removed most line loss (oval 0, s-bend 0.6, slalom 1.0), so sensor coverage is no longer the main limit. Iteration 2 moved the sensors to y=0.07 and cut body length to 0.12 m and mass to 0.6 kg. That dropped the score to 47.8, with s-bend progress falling from 0.163 to 0.119 and slalom score from 46.1 to 41.9. Lower yaw inertia and more sensor lead therefore did not help, and the y=0.05 layout should be kept. Body width cannot widen the limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m for every allowed body width. The remaining geometry lever for turn authority is wheel_track. Turn rate is (vR - vL)/wheel_track, so for the same PWM differential a narrower track turns faster. I therefore revert to iteration 1 and change only wheel_track, from 0.12 to 0.09 m (about 1.33x turn rate per unit of differential). Expected result: max_error and rms_error fall on the s-bend and slalom, progress rises above 0.2, and line-loss events stay at or below iteration 1. If progress stays near 0.12 with no change in max_error, the limit is base speed or controller gain, not geometry.
